title: Stick-on-stick technique learned from Mac Murray
summary: Russell describes Foster's way of striking one stick with the other to change tone, which Foster says Mac Murray also did; they compare stick sizes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Yes, yes. As I might describe how you're doing that, you're holding your sticks about the same as you always do. And you take your left hand and hit near the butt end, and sometimes of the right, and sometimes you hit up above your hand.

That's right. You hit on both. That's to make the stick change tone. If you notice, you notice your sticks are almost making notes. Yeah, that's right. So you got to know how to squeeze them to a certain extent to make them change the tone. Yeah. Now, you watch. Your left stick, they always hit right near the, between the tip and your hand.
